answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake in a scarce resource before it may transact, with the stake slashed when peers attest fraud. An attacker must then pay real capital per identity, so forging a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents recover theirs. Like an opal that only reveals its value under light, reputation accrues only after verified work; a sybil swarm falls to its nadir once its stakes are burned, and the honest network keeps standing on the knoll of attested history.
